config.title: What Happens on a Berlin Free Walking Tour: FAQ

items.q: Is a Berlin free walking tour really free?
items.a: On a tip-based walk you join without paying up front and tip the guide at the end what the walk was worth to you. There is no fixed price. My own walk no longer works that way: Berlin Then and Now costs €25 per person, paid when you book.

items.q: How long is the tour and how far do you walk?
items.a: My walk takes about 2.5 hours on foot and covers about 3 km, from the World Clock at Alexanderplatz to Hackescher Markt, with 11 stops covering 16 places. The route is mostly flat and the pace is built for looking rather than marching.

items.q: What do you actually see on the walk?
items.a: The historic core of the former East Berlin: the World Clock and TV Tower at Alexanderplatz, the Rotes Rathaus, St. Mary's Church, the Marx-Engels-Forum, Museum Island and the Berliner Dom, ending in the courtyards around Hackescher Markt. You can scrub through every stop on the timeline in this post before you book.

items.q: How much should I tip on a free walking tour in Berlin?
items.a: Tip what a guide's work and local knowledge were worth to you. There is no set figure and nothing is announced to the group. If you want a sense of the normal range beforehand, the tipping-in-Berlin guide covers it honestly.

At the World Clock (Weltzeituhr) on Alexanderplatz at 12:30. It is one of the easiest landmarks in the city to find, reachable by U-Bahn, S-Bahn, tram and bus. The exact spot is on the meeting point page, and the dates are on the booking page.
